story: As a study manager, I can filter the dashboard by study, region, and site status so I can focus review on a selected network slice.
acceptance_criteria: Every selected filter narrows all site and chart outputs; clearing a filter restores the corresponding rows.

story: As a recruitment lead, I can see counts from screened through retained so I can identify where candidates leave the funnel.
acceptance_criteria: The funnel shows screened, eligible, consented, randomized, and retained counts for the selected screening cohort.

story: As a study manager, I can compare monthly enrollment targets with actual randomizations so I can review pace over time.
acceptance_criteria: Monthly chart groups targets and randomizations by calendar month and respects the selected studies and regions.

story: As a site manager, I can see site/study attainment and an explained review flag so I can prioritize follow-up.
acceptance_criteria: Rows include target, randomized count, attainment, and the rule that triggered a bottleneck flag.

story: As a clinical operations analyst, I can compare screening failure and consent-cycle measures across sites so I can locate recruitment friction.
acceptance_criteria: The site table shows failure rate and median screening-to-consent days for the selected cohort.

story: As a stakeholder, I can export the filtered site report so I can use the same view in a review meeting.
acceptance_criteria: A CSV download contains the visible site metrics and selected study/site dimensions.

story: As a data steward, I can review the ETL issue log so I can understand what was repaired or excluded.
acceptance_criteria: The quality tab shows source/clean counts, issue categories, example records, and a downloadable issue log.

story: As a data engineer, I can remove duplicate screening IDs so one screening is not counted twice.
acceptance_criteria: The ETL keeps the first row per screening ID, logs later duplicates, and reports how many rows were removed.

story: As a data engineer, I can reject screenings without a valid site/trial assignment so reports do not include orphan records.
acceptance_criteria: Unknown assignments and mismatched trial/site keys are excluded and written to the quality issue log.

story: As a data steward, I can enforce event-date sequence rules so impossible consent, randomization, or withdrawal dates do not distort metrics.
acceptance_criteria: Invalid dates are cleared according to the screening-to-consent-to-randomization-to-withdrawal sequence and each correction is logged.

story: As an analyst, I can use PostgreSQL CTE and window-function examples so stakeholder reporting is reproducible.
acceptance_criteria: The SQL folder contains a funnel CTE, cumulative monthly totals with LAG/SUM windows, within-study RANK, and QA checks.

story: As a product reviewer, I can inspect the prioritized backlog and acceptance criteria so I can understand scope and delivery slices.
acceptance_criteria: The app and repository expose at least 12 sprint-prioritized stories with explicit, reviewable acceptance criteria.
